verifications.claim: Artemis II traveled at speeds up to approximately 25,000 mph during critical phases of its mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'maximum speed prediction for Artemis II to 24,661.21 mph'; R3: 'reenter the atmosphere at a blazing 25,000 miles per hour'; R5: 'estimated 25,000 mph'; R6: 'predicted to reach a maximum velocity of about 25,000 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm speeds around 25,000 mph during reentry, a critical phase.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '25,000 miles per hour (40,000 kilometers per hour)'; R2: '24,661 mph (39,668 kph)'; R4: 'more than 11 km/s (40,000 km/h)'
verifications.reasoning: Direct equivalence stated in sources; conversion is accurate.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'travelling at more than 11 km/s (40,000 km/h)'
verifications.reasoning: Source explicitly states reentry speed over 11 km/s, matching the conversion.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's peak speed of approximately 25,000 mph was achieved during the trans-lunar injection (TLI) burn to leave Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'maximum speed prediction... 24,661.21 mph... during the peak heating period of reentry'; R5: 'peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour'; R6: 'fastest speed... re-enter Earth's atmosphere'; R7: 'TLI burn... 39,472 kilometers (24,527 miles) per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Sources attribute peak speed (~24,661 mph) to reentry, not TLI (24,527 mph, slightly lower).

verifications.claim: Artemis II's peak speed of approximately 25,000 mph was achieved during the high-speed re-entry into Earth's atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'maximum speed... 24,661.21 mph... during... reentry'; R2: '24,661 mph'; R5: 'peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour'; R6: 'fastest speed... re-enter Earth's atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state peak speed during reentry at ~24,661-25,000 mph.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm mission occurred in April 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's SLS rocket reached over 17,000 mph to achieve orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'the Artemis II SLS rocket hit more than 17,000 mph. That's 22 times the speed of sound'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for SLS speed to orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's spacecraft traveled at roughly 24,500–25,000 mph to leave Earth's orbit during translunar injection (TLI).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'In the translunar injection (TLI) burn... 39,472 kilometers (24,527 miles) per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Exact speed at TLI matches the range.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's Orion capsule reached speeds of around 24,000 to 25,000 mph when re-entering the atmosphere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'top speed of about 24,000 mph'; R2: '24,661 mph'; R3: '25,000 miles per hour'; R5: '24,664 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm reentry speeds in the exact range.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's Orion capsule reached about Mach 32 when re-entering the atmosphere.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Mach 33'; R4: 'more than 30 times the speed of sound'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Mach 33 or >30; claim's 'about Mach 32' is close but not exact.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's Orion capsule re-entry created temperatures up to 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'temperatures as high as 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; 'peak of some 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; R3: 'withstand up to 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state heat shield endures up to 5,000°F during reentry.

verifications.claim: Artemis II used a free return trajectory.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of free return trajectory.

verifications.claim: Artemis II's free return trajectory allowed the spacecraft to use the moon's gravity for a return trip.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '“free return” trajectory harnesses the power of gravity to save on fuel'
verifications.reasoning: Source describes free return using gravity (implying moon's) for return.

verifications.claim: Artemis II had a final splashdown speed of about 19 mph.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: '19 mph (30 kph) splashdown'; R1: 'less than 20 mph'; R3: '17 mph'; R5: '20 mph'; R6: '17 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Sources vary slightly (17-20 mph), with one exactly 19 mph; 'about' fits but not uniform.
